rows.fidelity_note: The paper describes prescribed and solver-specific information flags and refers to their semantics. The formal definition only writes get-info with a keyword argument, leaving both the flag’s meaning and the solver’s response unspecified.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Command.tokens

rows.fidelity_note: At version 2.7 the formal reserved-word set excludes every predefined symbol in this list. This supports the distinction between predefined symbols and reserved words; their predefined meanings are not supplied by the lexical definition.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.reserved

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition admits each listed spelling as a simple symbol at version 2.7. It does not assign their predefined meanings, but it agrees that the spellings are not excluded as reserved words.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.simpleSymbol

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition recognizes exactly tab, line feed, carriage return, and space: character codes 9, 10, 13, and 32.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.whiteSpaceChar

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition recognizes exactly the two byte ranges printed here: 32–126 and 128–255. Unlike the broader Unicode wording in Section 3.1, this appendix production has the same finite bounds as the formal definition.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.printableChar

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition recognizes exactly the ASCII digits 0 through 9, with codes 48 through 57.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.digit

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition recognizes exactly the two ASCII letter ranges A through Z and a through z, with codes 65–90 and 97–122.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.letter

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition allows 0 by itself or a nonempty sequence of decimal digits whose first digit is not 0. Leading zeros are excluded from longer numerals.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.numeral

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition is a numeral, a decimal point, zero or more zeros, and another numeral. Thus there is at least one digit after the point, while zeros may begin the fractional part.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.decimal

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition requires the lowercase prefix #x followed by one or more digits or letters A–F or a–f. Only the hexadecimal digits are case-insensitive.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.hexadecimal

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition requires the lowercase prefix #b followed by one or more characters, each either 0 or 1.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.binary

rows.fidelity_note: Using the appendix’s byte-based character ranges, the formal definition permits whitespace and printable contents between double quotes, with every interior quote doubled. This matches the displayed lexical rule.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.string

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition replaces each doubled quote in the contents by one quote and leaves every other byte unchanged. This supplies the escape interpretation named in the production, separately from recognizing the literal’s delimiters.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.unescape

rows.fidelity_note: The selected production ends before its punctuation list and restrictions. The formal definition also specifies those characters, excludes an initial digit, and excludes reserved words; the complete source span is needed for an exact comparison.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.simpleSymbol

rows.fidelity_note: The quotation stops before the punctuation characters themselves. The formal definition gives their precise set, so the following lines of the production should be included.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.symbolPunctuation

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition is the second alternative: a vertical bar, then whitespace and printable characters other than a vertical bar or backslash, then a vertical bar. Its printable characters are the byte ranges Appendix B prints for that category.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.quotedSymbol

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition is the first alternative only, a simple symbol; the quoted alternative is a separate definition. Together the two give the production.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.simpleSymbol

rows.fidelity_note: The paper specifies a colon followed by a simple symbol; the formal definition also permits an initial digit or a reserved word after the colon, such as :56 or :let. This follows the older keyword rule and the paper’s own :56 example, rather than the displayed production literally.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Lexicon.keyword

rows.fidelity_note: The paper gives the complete pattern production; the formal definition requires a nonempty argument list for a constructor pattern and checks wildcard availability. Parentheses and the distinction between a single symbol and a constructor pattern are defined separately.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Pattern.Valid

rows.fidelity_note: The paper defines whole patterns; the formal definition only restricts the symbol-or-wildcard component, requiring version 2.7 for a wildcard. It says nothing about constructor patterns or their argument lists.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.SymbolOrWildcard.Valid

rows.fidelity_note: The paper requires at least one argument in a parenthesized constructor pattern; the formal definition also allows an empty argument list. A separate grammatical condition excludes that extra case.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Pattern

rows.fidelity_note: The paper defines both single-symbol patterns and constructor patterns; the formal definition supplies only a symbol or wildcard, the component used inside those patterns.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.SymbolOrWildcard

rows.fidelity_note: The formal definition writes the two pattern forms, but can also write a parenthesized constructor without arguments. The paper’s plus sign excludes that case, which is ruled out only by a separate grammatical condition.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.Pattern.tokens

rows.fidelity_note: The paper specifies complete patterns; the formal definition emits just a symbol or an underscore. This explains one pattern component rather than the whole production.
rows.name: BSmtLibSpec.Grammar.Tree.SymbolOrWildcard.token

topics.description: Source files are divided into lexical tokens, with whitespace and comments separating them.
topics.name: Source text and tokenization

topics.description: The lexical rules distinguish whitespace, printable characters, digits, and ASCII letters.
topics.name: Character classes

topics.description: Symbols, keywords, and reserved words supply the names and fixed vocabulary of the language.
topics.name: Symbols and reserved words

topics.description: Numerals, decimals, hexadecimal literals, and binary literals each have a prescribed spelling.
topics.name: Numeric literals

topics.description: Double quotes delimit strings, and doubling an interior quote gives the language’s single lexical escape.
topics.name: String literals

topics.description: Flat constructor patterns, variable patterns, and wildcards describe the cases of a match expression.
topics.name: Pattern matching

topics.description: Terms combine constants, identifiers, applications, abstractions, quantifiers, local definitions, matches, and annotations.
topics.name: Term grammar

topics.description: Local variable declarations associate names with terms or sorts and determine the scope of their occurrences.
topics.name: Variables and scope

topics.description: Attributes attach additional information to a term without changing its logical meaning.
topics.name: Term annotations

topics.description: An attribute consists of a keyword with an optional special constant, symbol, or parenthesized list as its value.
topics.name: Attribute syntax

topics.description: Command productions specify their arguments, including option attributes and information flags.
topics.name: Command syntax and options

topics.description: Scripts sequence commands that control a solver and request its responses.
topics.name: Scripts and solver interaction

topics.description: Sort, datatype, constructor, selector, and function declarations describe the components introduced by commands.
topics.name: Declarations and definitions

topics.description: Special constants and other atoms combine into possibly empty parenthesized S-expressions.
topics.name: S-expressions and constants

topics.description: Identifiers are symbols, optionally qualified by one or more numeral or symbol indices.
topics.name: Indexed identifiers

topics.description: Sort expressions are identifiers, optionally applied to one or more sort expressions.
topics.name: Sort expressions
